ryan: alerted by SLO pager — 99th latency for shared-gpu-pool jumped from 120ms -> 980ms around 03:12 UTC. seeing sustained tail for ~6m. looks like noisy neighbor but kernel logs weird. any takers?

sam: on it. linking profiler dumps now. suspecting kernel re-select churn when batch size fluctuates.

maria: can you paste the tail profile? curious about KV cache misses and kernel change events.

ryan: pasted initial snippet from runtime trace:```
[03:12:01] request id=abcd shard=gpupool-7 kernel=matmul_q8 run_ms=1.2
[03:12:01] request id=efgh shard=gpupool-7 kernel=matmul_q4 run_ms=45.6 (fallback to generic)
[03:12:02] kernel_switch event: matmul_q8 -> matmul_q4 reason=batch_estimate_high
[03:12:02] kv_cache_miss id=abcd keylen=128
[03:12:03] batch_coalesce delay=28ms cause=slot_wait
```

sam: hmm kernel_switch on short timescale. batching heuristics probably overreacting to transient queue depth. when kernel flips to q4 we lose optimized kernels and latency spikes.

pavan: from infra metrics, that pool had a spike in small high-priority tails from tenant:analytics_prod. they sent many long-context requests and a handful of tiny requests around same time. mixing long+short sequences causes our batch estimator to bump seq len and select heavier kernels.

maria: that fits. KV cache pressure shows eviction rate + re-pop events. when long reqs miss KV, they force recompute, bumping runtime and causing other short requests to wait -> slot_wait.

devops: infra-bot reports GPU memory pages around 85% and PCIe bandwidth saturated for 45s. also saw occasional recompile attempts from autotuner.

infra-bot: [auto] Rollout note: autoscaler bumped capacity +1 at 03:13:05 but new instance not yet warmed for optimized kernels.

ryan: so root causes: 1) mixed length workload from one noisy tenant, 2) batching heuristic over-corrects kernel selection, 3) KV cache churn + autotuner triggers -> fallback kernels. any quick mitigations?

sam: short-term: apply per-tenant soft isolation: cap concurrent small-request tokens for analytics_prod to 30% of pool. also pause autotuner on affected nodes to avoid recompiles mid-spike.

maria: mid-term: change batching heuristic to require stable sequence-length estimate over X ms before switching kernels (suggest 200ms window). also add decay to kernel confidence so single transient long request doesn't flip entire shard.

pavan: agree. also recommend proactive KV pinning for heavy long-context tenants to avoid eviction storms — or increase KV slot reservation for dedicated tenants.

ryan: i pushed a quick config change: paused autotuner on gpupool-7 and applied tenant soft-cap. initial tail dropped to ~220ms within 90s. will watch for regressions.

sam: filing a perf incident follow-up with repro steps and profiling artifacts. plan: reproduce locally with mixed seq simulator, run `runtime-profiler --trace kernel_switch --kv-events` for 10m.

maria: add unit test for batching estimator: simulate oscillating sequence-length pattern and assert kernel stability. Also add e2e test that ensures small requests never see >200ms added wait due to large-request oscillation.

devops: rolling a patch to autotuner to add jitter thresholds before compile. putting canary on 2 nodes.

ryan: good. Owners: sam (investigation + heuristic PR), maria (tests + KV pin strategy), pavan (autoscaler/tenant caps), devops (autotuner patch). ETA 3 days for PRs, 1 day for hotfix config.

pavan: logging note: we should add a condensed event log for kernel_switch + kv_eviction with per-request IDs to make triage faster. filing ticket INF-768.

sam: repro logs + sim harness link: https://redwood.internal/sim/seq-mix-2026 attach: profiler_dump_2360001111.tar.gz

ryan: thanks all :thumbsup: keeping thread open until postmortem doc.

infra-bot: [auto] Incident: perf-spike-2360001111 -> status: mitigated -> next: postmortem draft.

maria: postmortem checklist: timeline, root cause, mitigation, long-term fixes, test coverage, rollout plan. I'll start the draft.

ryan: closing actions logged in issue PERF-4292. will update when postmortem ready.
